definitions.gloss: Go; the board game of Go
definitions.explanation: A strategic board game played with black and white stones on a 19×19 grid, where players compete to control territory. One of the oldest and most respected board games in East Asia.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{毎週|まいしゅう}{囲碁|いご}{教室|きょうしつ}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: My grandfather goes to Go classes every week.

examples.japanese: {囲碁|いご}の{世界|せかい}{大会|たいかい}で{日本|にほん}の{棋士|きし}が{優勝|ゆうしょう}した。
examples.english: A Japanese Go player won the world championship.

notes:
{囲碁|いご} is the Japanese name for the board game Go, one of the oldest strategy games in the world. Often shortened to just {碁|ご} in casual speech.

KEY VOCABULARY:
- {碁盤|ごばん}: Go board
- {碁石|ごいし}: Go stones
- {対局|たいきょく}: match, game
- {棋士|きし}: professional Go player
- {段|だん}: rank (e.g., {初段|しょだん}, {九段|くだん})
- {手|て}: a move

USAGE:
The verb for playing Go is {打|う}つ (to play/strike), not する: {碁|ご}を{打|う}つ. This is shared with {将棋|しょうぎ}.

WATCH OUT:
Not to be confused with {以後|いご} (from now on, hereafter) — same reading, different kanji and meaning.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Go has a long tradition in Japan. The {日本棋院|にほんきいん} (Nihon Ki-in) is the main professional organization.
